brief: NVDA's Board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO this morning, a move the note says was orchestrated by the Trump Administration; the President was publicly discussing his involvement as the note was written. The Board said senior US government input leaves it confident Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk. The note argues Huang's return restores strategic vision, relationships and employee morale, and that Administration backing, a continuing Board investigation into Huang being targeted by foreign intelligence, a new National Security and Export Control Committee, and a new Chief Compliance Officer will calm investor fears over alleged improper China sales, for which the note says no evidence has been presented; it still expects a Congressional inquiry from the incoming Democratic Congress. SE Asia and Brazilian data center shipments became subject to new export controls last week, not prohibited before; NVDA holds that since demand still exceeds supply, impact is insignificant, though the note urges more geographic and customer disclosure to reassure investors. The note also expects continued scrutiny of future NVDA financing deals despite Huang's return, views CEO-CFO tension on this as proper, and likens NVDA's approach to AVGO's: such financing is meant as a short-term bridge until neocloud and frontier-model customers mature.
